# `start_create_calib_frame`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the calibration-frame creation worker (automatic or custom bias/flat).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (D64 and D32 command-socket invocation) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, start_create_calib_frame @0xdd0e0, StartCreateCalib @0x3bc420, CreateCalib @0x3bafa0 (slot write @0x3bb478, release on failure @0x3bb8f8, @0x3bb984, @0x3bba00, @0x3bba20), CreateCalibFunc @0x3bbb30 (save @0x3bbcf0), AppCreateCalibFunc @0x3bbe70 (64-bit build) |

Refused with 524 first if a View function, ViewPlan, planet stack, batch stack or any mount-occupying function is active. Then initialises the shared calibration parameters, optionally creates the customer library directory, and starts a named worker. Success acknowledges the start, not the creation of any file. With wide_cam the request is relayed to the peer process first. Progress is reported by CreateCalibFrame function events; only the custom path adds exp_us, adu and type. Each new bias or flat replaces the in-memory frame of its kind as soon as it finishes, before the file is written and regardless of customer_library; a failed or stopped run empties the in-memory frame of the kind being built.

Side effects: Initialises the shared calibration state, may run a directory creation for the customer library, selects the automatic or custom worker and starts it. Synchronous setup with no explicit short timeout, then asynchronous capture. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_create_calib_frame"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Object only; absent, null, scalar or array params behave as an empty object (no positional form). Unknown keys are ignored. exp_us, adu_min and adu_max are read only when type is a string. [READ] |
| `params.wide_cam` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Target the wide camera. Wrong type is treated as false. true requires wide-camera star view support (else 210); the request is relayed to the peer process before the remaining parsing. [READ] |
| `params.customer_library` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Write into the customer library (a directory may be created). A present value of another type gives 106. [READ] |
| `params.type` | string | no | - | Calibration kind. The literal bias selects bias; any other string selects flat (with a filter wheel, the wheel position decides the flat kind). Missing or non-string selects the automatic calibration worker. Not the same enum as the frame type used by set_calib_frame. [READ] |
| `params.exp_us` | integer | no | - | Exposure in microseconds. Missing or wrong type is logged and left at -1 (device default). No parser bound. [READ] |
| `params.adu_min` | integer | no | - | Lower ADU bound. Custom ranges must satisfy 0 <= adu_min <= adu_max <= 60000, else 204. If either ADU key is missing or mistyped, BOTH are replaced by defaults (flat: 10000 to 40000; bias: 0 to the dark threshold). [READ] |
| `params.adu_max` | integer | no | - | Upper ADU bound; see adu_min. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 524 | A View function, ViewPlan, planet stack, batch stack or mount-occupying function is active; checked before parsing | `function conflict` |
| 210 | wide_cam requested but the model does not support wide star view | `not supported` |
| 106 | customer_library present with a type other than boolean or integer (local path) | `expected bool param` |
| 318 | Camera not opened | `device not connected` |
| 268 | A calibration worker is already running | `operation is in progress` |
| 204 | Invalid calibration kind or ADU range | `out of limit` |
| 218 | Customer directory could not be created or accessed | `fail to write file` |
| 300 | Relay with no caller context | `internal error` |
| 207 | Flat-kind lookup failed for an invalid wheel position | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Thread-start and peer errors are forwarded and not fully enumerated. A relay failure can append a second error fragment to the reply.

## Example

Request, auto - Automatic calibration into the customer library (shape OBSERVED in app encoder analysis; values invented):

```json
{"id":51,"method":"start_create_calib_frame","params":{"customer_library":true}}
```

Request, custom-flat - Custom flat with an ADU window:

```json
{"id":52,"method":"start_create_calib_frame","params":{"wide_cam":false,"type":"flat","customer_library":true,"exp_us":20000,"adu_min":10000,"adu_max":40000}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_create_calib_frame","result":0,"code":0,"id":51}
```

Reply, conflict:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_create_calib_frame","error":"function conflict","code":524,"id":53}
```
